newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 26.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The Cabinet today will approve the bill abolishing tax exemptions, radically changing the face of Greek taxation and bringing in an expected 130 billion drachmas in revenue. The bill foresees the full abolition of tax breaks for the president, MPs and others in public office, as well as for journalists. Provisions for reduced taxation on bonuses to tax, customs, military and police officials will go, and will be pared down for seamen and Olympic Airways pilots.
--The European Union hurries through the abolition of monopolies in telecommunications, wanting Greece's OTE to give up its monopoliy in the year 2000 rather than 2003 as orginally agreed.
--The National Bank of Greece's first branch in Tirana began operating yesterday; a National Bank branch is expected to open in Bucharest soon.
IMERISIA
--The government reveals its cards today at the Cabinet meeting to approve the new packjage of economic measures bringing in one trillion drachmas in revenues.

--The latest half-yearly report by the national economy ministry indicates a significant step will have been taken towards convergecne by 1998, but the Greek economy will still not be ready theyn for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

--The national economy and labour ministries, along with the European Commission, plan incentives for businesses in specially created zones around the country. Reduced working hours and insurance contributions and local vocational training programmes will be available in the zones.
--The secondary bond market sees increased demand and a rise in prices following Friday's successful bond auction, probably one of the last tax-free issues.
KERDOS

--The state hopes for 25 billion drachmas from the real estate tax, setting property valued at 60 million drachmas as the tax threshold for each individual and 150 million for a four-member family, according to sources.
-- National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou: 1997 will be a year of the privatisation of smaller banks and ailing firms.
--Procedures to sell off four ailing firms are stepped up, sources say.
EXPRESS

--The European Investment Bank's vice-president Panayiotis Yennimatas dismisses claims that Greece will be close to Maastricht criteria in 1998. Yennimatas says Greece may achieve the criteria in a five-year programme because the economic and social infrastructure cannot bear the burden of a speedier programme.
--Taxes will be significantly higher for self-employed professionals and businesses this year due to the adjustment of objective tax criteria.
--National economy ministry report claims that Greece can achieve Maastricht targets by 1998 if the government follows the same mixture of economic policies.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The Capital Market Commission will examine the fact today that at least 30 brokerage firms have not promptly informed the Athens Stock Exchange of share transfers.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
